reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate. (1) No matched-budget null: 'random median' vs annealed top-5 conflates optimisation with regression to the mean/winner's curse; need best-of-600 random arm and a shuffled-objective anneal arm. (2) Metric is an F4 max-degree/matrix-size from msolve on one or few targets: a proxy, noisy per target, not the certified last fall degree; matrix size is a different quantity from degree and 4x smaller is dominated by sat/unsat and #solutions. (3) Integer-valued, near-constant objective: measured with prebuilt hky_last_fall_degree at n=19 (random family, 20 draws, rand and sat targets) d_last=4, e0=4, ffd=2 on EVERY draw (only DG/nsol/ideal_dims vary by 2-6 dims in ~4046), so the random 5-95% band is a single value; 'mean >=1 below random median' is impossible/undefined and annealing has no gradient (plateau). Prior programme result: d_F<=k+2, certified >=5 at n=33-45, presentation-dependent, so n=19 sits at floor. (4) l=5 at n=19 gives 2l=10 unknowns vs 19 equations: almost every target is UNSAT, so the measured quantity is a refutation degree, not a decomposition-solving degree; tool's own convention is nprime=(n-1)/2=9 (SAT ~2 s/draw there). (5) Scaling: a single (n,l) says nothing about n=131; Diem-style win needs d_F bounded in n, requiring >=3 n values and a trend; subspace search by measurement is infeasible at n=131 so only a recognised structural feature of the optimiser's output can transfer. (6) Fresh-target generalisation is a good idea (kept). CPU: msolve on 10-var Boolean is fast (~0.2 s) so 600x(multi-target) is about 10-20 min, tight but runnable; hky SAT at l=9 is 2 s/draw so 600 draws exceed budget; use UNSAT/rand targets (~0.25 s/draw) or l=5-7.
fix: Redesign: (a) Metric = certified d_last/e0 and closure_dims/ideal_dims gap from prebuilt hky_last_fall_degree (cell --n N --family random --target rand|sat --draws K --seed S --cmax C), secondary = msolve -v 2 -g 2 max F4 deg and largest matrix on SAME polys; report rank/dim counts, never wall time. Objective for annealing = a continuous structural score (e.g. ideal_dims[c]-closure_dims[c] at the degree below d_last, or fraction of targets with d_last<=3), because d_last is an integer plateau. (b) Arms with equal evaluation budget B=600: A random best-of-600 (null), B anneal (300 random seeds + 300 moves, single-basis-vector flips/ F2-linear changes), C anneal on a label-shuffled/random-permuted objective (selection-noise control), D structured baselines already known (subfield-like/low-weight/polynomial-basis subspaces). Pre-register: success iff arm B top-5 on 20 FRESH targets (disjoint seeds, matched sat/unsat mix) has mean d_last (or structural score) below the 5th percentile of arm A top-5 and below arm C, via permutation test over subspaces. (c) First do a 2-minute variance pilot at each cell: if random d_last has zero variance (as at n=19, l=9) abort that cell as uninformative and move to a cell with spread (n=33-45 per programme data, l small, cmax>=6) or to unmeasured m=4 cells. (d) Scaling arm: repeat pilot-sized version at n in {13,17,19,23,29} (primes, ord_n(2) large) with l=(n-1)/2 and l=5; claim n-independence only if optimum d_last stays flat while random median grows; otherwise class as constant-factor/engineering. (e) State up front: toy result is evidence about d_F growth only, not n=131; the idea is 'advance' only if the gap grows with n or the optimiser output has an identifiable invariant; otherwise engineering. (f) Budget: pilot 3 min, main arms 12 min at ~0.25 s/draw (rand targets, l<=7) or reduce draws; keep under 19 CPU-min.
